questions.q: In this lab, why was `gs.info()` placed right after `gr.query()`, before looking at the `while` loop at all?
options: Because the Script Debugger cannot be used on Script Includes under any circumstances
To confirm the query was even finding any records before suspecting the logic that processes the results
Because `gs.info()` is required syntax for every GlideRecord query to run
To automatically fix the bug without needing to read any code
questions.explain: Tracing the query first rules out (or confirms) the data-fetch step before spending time inspecting the loop that consumes its results.

questions.q: The System Log showed this line: "Query returned 0 rows for risk: high" — even though matching Change Requests definitely existed. What does that rule out?
options: Nothing; the log line is unrelated to diagnosing the bug
It proves the Business Rule calling the method was never triggered
The `while` loop and `results.push()` call — since zero rows were returned, the bug has to be in the query itself
It proves the Script Include method doesn't exist
questions.explain: A row count of 0 means execution never reached anything past the query — the loop and push logic are irrelevant to a bug that never gets that far.

questions.q: What was the actual bug in `gr.addEncodedQuery('active=ture^risk=' + riskLevel)`?
options: The Script Include class was never registered with `Class.create()`
`addEncodedQuery()` does not accept the `^` character
A typo — `ture` instead of `true` — which silently matches zero records instead of throwing an error
The `riskLevel` variable was never defined anywhere
questions.explain: The encoded query parser doesn't validate the value `ture` against anything — it just never matches, since no record literally has that active value.

questions.q: Why didn't the encoded query typo `active=ture` throw a script error that would have pointed directly at the bug?
options: ServiceNow's encoded query parser doesn't reject unrecognized values — it just matches zero records silently
`active=ture` is actually valid syntax with a different meaning than `active=true`
GlideRecord throws an error for any typo, so this scenario couldn't actually happen
Encoded queries are validated at save time and this one would have been rejected
questions.explain: This is exactly why the gs.info() row-count trace mattered — a silent zero-match failure gives no error to point at the problem on its own.

questions.q: After changing `active=ture` to `active=true`, what's the correct next step per this lab?
options: Re-run the same gs.info() trace to confirm the row count is no longer zero, then remove the temporary logging
Immediately delete the entire Script Include method, since it's now unnecessary
Leave the debug gs.info() calls permanently in the production script
Assume the fix worked without checking, since the typo is obviously the only possible bug
questions.explain: Verifying with the same trace confirms the fix actually worked, and cleaning up temporary logging avoids adding noise to the System Log going forward.
